Decision draft · Calendar 2027 · Analysis 16 October 2026

Build capability in stages.
Use coverage to guide the plan, and practical evidence to gate progression.

Four alternatives for the cyber organisation, calculated from catalogue v8 and the existing capability model. Recommended: a quality-focused core with a five-hour foundation, followed by role-specific practice and assessment.

01 · The decision

Recommend Option 4; retain Option 1 as the coverage benchmark

Option 4 trades 4.8 percentage points of foundation coverage against Option 1 for better cyber-role fit, explicit agent-safety reading, and fewer wholly uncovered critical foundation requirements. It uses 4h48m of foundation resources within a proposed 5h cap. The Practitioner, Expert and specialist course caps stay at 8h, 24h and 4h.

These are teaching-evidence percentages, not proficiency or readiness scores. Completing the curriculum does not establish that a learner can supervise or secure agents. Internal exercises and observed sign-off are required; they receive no automatic coverage credit.

Inherited courses contribute where relevant. Each column uses its own applicable requirements and equal weight per need; do not average these columns into one workforce score. Expert values include N5.7 and the relevant role preset.

OPTION 1

Benchmark, not rollout

Highest mathematical coverage within the original budgets. It leaves N5 AI-powered threats at 0% in foundation and selects a helping-professions course and several brief surveys. Audience tags do not prove role fit.

OPTION 2

Use if 4h is immovable

Named instructors, useful practice and distinct purposes. Drops marginal observability courses. Foundation remains especially thin on agent anatomy and safety components: N2 is 0%.

OPTION 3

Use for a strict sourcing policy

Only first-party, public-agency, established training-provider and recognised professional-community resources. More readings, weaker work-redesign coverage. Reputation is not proof of practical learning.

OPTION 4

Recommended, subject to Q1 pilot

Same role pathways as Option 2; adds the full CERT-FR agent-risk bulletin to foundation. Only the foundation course cap changes, from 4h to 5h. Improves agent/control awareness and removes three critical zero-score gaps for one extra planned hour.

Annual learner commitment, including inherited learning

Hours below include course/reading time plus planned internal learning, practice and assessment. They exclude optional specialties, certification extensions, remedial repeats and provider costs. Technical and Governance Expert are alternative paths, not compulsory consecutive levels. Leadership inherits foundation directly.

Role-fit adaptations: TR-100 includes code labs and SEC495 requires intermediate Python. For a non-coding Practitioner, replace TR-100 with a bank-owned no-code evaluation harness and 3h extra assisted practice. The resulting planned total is 18.8h; recorded Practitioner-layer coverage falls from 48.3% to 33.3% until the internal alternative is assessed. Do not award full-course coverage for watching a demonstration. Use a readiness diagnostic before the technical path and fund prerequisites separately if needed.

Scope: this is a first-year capability uplift, not a promise that every learner becomes an autonomous-agent engineer. SEC495 develops RAG/agentic-RAG skills; it is not a complete platform-engineering programme. Keep higher-risk designs outside individual authorisation until further evidence is obtained.

TR-127 is a French-language bulletin. Validate accessibility; an approved equivalent translation may be required. It is a targeted awareness reading, not an incident-response lab. CERT-FR source

03 · Review and adapt

Inspect every proposed course and its evidence

Choose any option and cohort. Resource time is incremental; cumulative totals include ancestors once. “Unique coverage points” is the loss in this cohort’s score if that resource is removed from the current selection. It is not a measurement of video-content duplication or learner benefit.

04 · Why these choices

Review each course, not just its provider brand

Options 2 and 4 use a desk review of role fit, published content, instructor identity, practical tasks, assessment and distinct outcomes. I have not completed these courses. A full syllabus gives stronger evidence for scoring; it does not prove teaching quality. No arbitrary numerical “quality multiplier” has been applied to the workbook scores.

DecisionReason and consequence
Keep INT-437 and INT-2787 provisionallyDistinct strands: AI mental models/limitations and cyber social-engineering threats. Named instructors and application activities; not strong independent skill assessment. Confirm the exact enterprise versions and language fit in the pilot.
Omit INT-334 from the quality coreStrong scored efficiency, but examples are for therapists/coaches and helping professions. Transfer to cyber work is less direct. This is a role-fit decision, not a finding that the course is poor.
Omit INT-1099 and INT-1473 from the coreA banking architecture walkthrough and a 59-minute evaluation survey add recorded coverage, but are weak substitutes for observed supervision and evaluation practice. Keep available as targeted references.
One core evaluation environment: TR-100Avoid stacking the Galileo course INT-2041 (7h29m) and additional Langfuse/observability courses without a tool-adoption reason. Their full durations still apply even where syllabuses overlap. Score maxima already remove duplicate requirement credit; syllabus review addresses actual teaching repetition.
Keep INT-194 for technical rolesConcrete exploit/fix work, RBAC and tool-boundary controls. Requires an approved sandbox and review of its cloud dependencies; ungraded exercises need the bank sign-off.
INT-397, not INT-397 plus INT-1840Under the current scores, adding INT-1840 gives no extra N13 coverage. Governance learners receive the practical governance scorecard and a bank-specific evidence challenge.
INT-2478 is the most provisional choiceIts templates and role plays uniquely support N14. Confirm the enterprise content and pilot it before rollout. Removing it from the recommended technical pathway reduces layer coverage from 57.7% to 45.7%, and N14 from 73.3% to 13.3%. An internal replacement must earn new evidence; it cannot inherit these scores.
Move TR-094 to technical rolesMCP construction is useful for builders; adding it to the selected Practitioner core yields no extra scored coverage. The syllabus does not establish secure authorisation practice, so retain the security exercise.
Treat standards, reports and guides as readingsNIST, OWASP, ANSSI, CSA and Microsoft references are credible source material, not assessed hands-on training. OWASP ACS is an early specification and CSA autonomy levels are a proposal; neither becomes bank policy automatically.
Q1 release criteria — proposed: pilot with 5–10 representative learners across technical and non-technical roles. Review the exact purchased version, working labs, accuracy, time, accessibility and overlap. Require completion of an independent scenario task, not a satisfaction rating alone. Replace content with material inaccuracies or unusable exercises, then recalculate coverage. Assign one curriculum owner to maintain the decision log.

Provider checks include INT-437, INT-194, INT-397 and the TR-100 course outline. INT-2478 remains provisional; publicly accessible cached descriptions do not verify the current enterprise version.

07 · A realistic 2027 sequence

Deliver in waves and release authority through observed gates

Q1 · Validate & begin

Agree the plan and pilot

Heads nominate roles and exemptions. Validate source versions, licences, French-language access and coding prerequisites. Pilot 5–10 learners; build and calibrate the internal exercises. Start foundation.

Q2 · Foundation & supervisors

Complete Gate 1; teach L2

Finish the 7.8h foundation in short sessions. Start Practitioner learning for nominated supervisors; use two labs and an observed check. Stagger cohorts around operational peaks.

Q3 · Expert pathways

Apply learning to a real use case

After Gate 2, technical and governance candidates take their relevant resources and scoped capstones. Heads assign only the necessary specialty branch. Use an approved environment and synthetic or approved data.

Q4 · Challenge & authorise

Independent assessment and refresh

Complete capstone challenge and remediation, record permitted action classes and refresh on material tool/model changes. Review operational results and plan 2028 depth. Leadership forums run quarterly.

GateProposed evidenceDecision owner
G1 · Safe userSuggested knowledge threshold 80%, plus every safety-critical case correct. Demonstrate allowed data/tool choices and escalation. Calibrate this threshold in the pilot.Domain training lead with IDP/security policy owner
G2 · Agent supervisorObserved pass on all critical checklist actions, including independent checking, stop/revoke and fallback. Complete a Skill lifecycle record and known-answer evaluation. Failed safety steps require remediation and a new attempt.Domain Expert and operational tool owner
G3 · Role-specific ExpertIndependent challenge of a functioning technical implementation or governance evidence dossier; reproduce failures and justify controls. Record residual gaps and the exact approved operating scope.Expert assessor independent of the candidate’s project, with domain head approval

External credentials can be additional evidence; none grants blanket operational authority. Existing competence may be challenged through the same gate instead of repeating a course, with the exemption recorded. The model’s L1/L2/L3 labels are responsibilities, not automatic promotions awarded by course completion.

Capacity: the recommended technical path is about one hour per working week on average before specialties, but project and assessment sessions need protected blocks. The totals are base commitments, not guarantees of mastery. Published video runtimes are not measured elapsed learner time: pausing, provider exercises and prerequisites can add time. Measure these in the pilot and revise budgets before rollout. Reserve a separate 20% scheduling contingency for remediation and disruption; do not count that reserve as completed learning. Content creation, sandbox provision, facilitator/assessor capacity and licence costs require a separate team budget.

Head flexibility: keep the shared safety gate; allow substitutions and role-scoping changes with a short rationale. Recalculate score, critical gaps and hours; check distinct learning outcomes and the actual licence version. Record the owner, applicability, bank exercise and evidence gate. Use the full catalogue for discovery. Courses outside the curated shortlist remain visible in the planner, but must be unexcluded for automatic recommendations.

Measure outcomes: track completion, first-pass and reassessment results, trace-review accuracy, time to stop/revoke, quality of Skill ownership records, reproducibility of evaluations, and evidence-based risk decisions. Report failures and remediation without treating high course coverage as success.

08 · Where credentials add value

Use a targeted certification route, not one exam for every level

Option 3 satisfies the reputable-source restriction without requiring an exam. The following are optional extensions for nominated staff. They have not been inserted into the four core scenarios, and their exam results do not change the teaching scores.

RouteProposed use and commitmentCoverage / gating judgement
All staff · course completion certificateAnthropic AI Fluency (TR-089, budget 4h) offers a completion certificate. Vanderbilt TR-165 (4h) is another reputable option with assignments. Treat either as a replacement or explicitly budgeted alternative, not an uncosted extra.A completion certificate supports engagement, not a bank-specific safety or agent-supervision licence. Neither is a universal cybersecurity professional certification.
Practitioner · CompTIA SecAI+ extensionAdd the Pluralsight prep path TR-155 to Option 3’s Practitioner core. Current four module durations sum to 9h26m (catalogue metadata says 8h). Raise the Practitioner course cap to 14h; with 6h estimated revision and 1h catalogue exam allowance, cumulative learner commitment is about 33.9h. Confirm exam format at booking.The N4.7/N7–N9 layer remains 48.3%; the path improves some inherited fundamentals, taking cumulative coverage to 45.9%. It is valuable broad certification preparation, not evidence that N7 supervision is complete. Gate 2 still applies.
Technical specialist · SANS SEC545 / GIAC GAIPSReplace Option 3’s 11h technical core with SEC545 (30h) plus TR-063 (2h). Add 8h initial revision allowance and the current 2h exam. With inherited learning and 12h internal technical work, plan about 71.4h cumulatively. This variant does not also include SecAI+.Technical-layer coverage is 48.6% under the existing scores, versus 50.2% for the shorter Option 3 core. The attraction is deeper security labs and an external assessment, not higher coverage of every organisational need. Requires explicit time and licence funding.
Red-team specialist · SEC536 / GAIPTSEC536 has an 18h self-paced course duration; this exceeds the standard 4h specialist cap before exam or revision. Use for a small number of designated offensive-AI specialists.Do not prescribe it to every AppSec practitioner. Budget the complete preparation and external exam separately; retain the bank containment/trajectory gate.
Governance / assurance · AAISM or AAIAAAISM requires active CISM or CISSP. AAIA requires active CISA or a qualifying advanced audit credential with an IT-audit focus. Confirm individual eligibility and scope a complete prep package.Good targeted credentials for eligible roles; not a default ladder for all staff. The catalogue’s certification records do not justify awarding full scored coverage to unassessed prep materials, and ambiguous training days do not provide a reliable hours total.

Primary sources: Anthropic AI Fluency; Vanderbilt course; Pluralsight SecAI+ path; SEC545; GAIPS exam; SEC536; AAISM; AAIA prerequisites. Checked 16 October 2026; recheck before 2027 procurement.

Keep the proposed plan separate from the source assessment

The active snapshot was reconciled to 7,084 workbook course/need results. The capability model and workbook remain unchanged. Existing tool-track entries without assessments are not assigned inferred scores.

  1. For each requirement, use the maximum recorded score across selected and inherited courses. Missing assessments contribute zero mathematically and remain labelled unassessed; an explicit assessed zero is different.
  2. For each need, divide the score sum by 3 × applicable requirement count. Average needs equally within each cohort. Do not combine independent options, average cumulative cohorts or infer a workforce average without headcounts.
  3. Option 1 uses the app’s HiGHS mixed-integer optimisation: coverage first, then fewer hours, then fewer resources, with original audience eligibility, usable full durations and the 4/8/24/4h course budgets. All 17 solves were proven optimal conditional on preceding inherited selections. This is not a global optimum across all functions. Options 2–4 are curated proposals, not mathematical optima.
  4. Use full-course durations; ranges use their upper bound. Readings are identified as readings. The 6h NIST bundle duration is a planner estimate and should be piloted; shortening it does not retain full-bundle scores automatically. No excerpt receives its parent course’s complete score.
  5. Scenarios carry planning-only duration corrections: TR-158 “1h30” = 1.5h; TR-155 = 9h26m from its current published modules; explicit minute durations are retained for INT-271/275/276/340/452/476/1473 where lecture-count text confused the parser. TR-159 has per-collection durations but no full collection total and remains excluded. These corrections do not rescore the catalogue or change the app source.
  6. Internal hours are proposed learner commitments. Planned activities do not close assessed gaps. Development and instructor effort, headcounts, licence entitlements, business peaks, prerequisites and exam retries are not known and require head-level planning.

Independent Python verification reconciled all 68 cohort calculations, per-requirement maxima, equal-need weighting, inheritance and deduplicated hours; confirmed source workbook bytes against the snapshot hash; and checked all course budgets. It also confirmed that INT-397 plus INT-1840 adds no N13 coverage.

Decisions for heads: approve the 5h shared-resource cap and protected internal time; nominate supervisors/Experts and the relevant specialist branches; appoint internal-content owners and assessors; validate coding/language/licence access; decide whether the firm requires the reputable-only sourcing route; and fund any credential exceptions. Start with the exact course lists, then change them with a recorded rationale.

Use this pack

Open this HTML directly in a browser; it needs neither Node nor Python. All analysis data is embedded and processed locally. External navigation happens only when a source or course link is opened. Unzip the complete pack into one folder to use the companion JSON/CSV download links below. Import the desired scenario JSON into the existing Training Planner to edit selections and applicability; no saved app scenario is overwritten by this report. For printing, the browser prints the currently selected cohort’s detail plus the comparison and plan.
